entries.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drones in Libya, Zelensky says
entries.snippet: The Kremlin warns of an "escalation of tensions in the region", but declines to comment directly on the attacks in Libya.

entries.title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed
entries.snippet: The prime minister of Australia, which co-hosted COP31, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".

entries.title: Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says
entries.snippet: The report says there are signs of possible contamination across almost all of Gaza as a result of Israel's actions.

entries.title: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
entries.snippet: Eleven people are dead in the attack on Dymer, with rescue efforts ongoing to find those still missing from the residential building.

entries.title: Flights grounded in Belgium due to strike against austerity measures
entries.snippet: A series of strikes have hit Belgium in recent months as the prime minister struggles to agree a budget to cut costs.

entries.title: Presidential villa also hit by water and power cuts, Nigerian leader says
entries.snippet: Bola Tinubu says he was shaving last week when the water cut out - an experience familiar to many Nigerians.

entries.title: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
entries.snippet: The couple have been together for four years and were engaged in 2025.

entries.title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore ties after tensions over conflict
entries.snippet: The two leaders committed to upholding sovereignty and "non-interference in the internal affairs of states".

entries.title: Russia-bound ship towed away after it was attacked in Gulf of Finland
entries.snippet: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone strike on Saturday. Kyiv has yet to comment.

entries.title: South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal
entries.snippet: Choi Kyo-jin admits last-minute measures to stop AI-assisted cheating during the college entrance exam caused chaos.

entries.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
entries.snippet: Democrats have now won at least 258 seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats.

entries.title: US Army to detonate tonnes of unstable explosives in Iowa despite court order
entries.snippet: The Army says "swift action" is necessary to protect its personnel and nearby communities around its ammunition plant in Iowa.

entries.title: Three killed and dozens missing after fire at Indonesian factory
entries.snippet: At least three people were killed and many more feared dead after a fire at a confectionary factory.

entries.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
entries.snippet: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.

entries.title: Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89
entries.snippet: In a statement to Italian media, his family remember him as "the greatest jeweller of our time".

entries.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
entries.snippet: The National Crime Information Center database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information.

entries.title: Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
entries.snippet: The hair was given as a sign of friendship shortly before Washington's death in 1799, according to a descendent of its former owner.

entries.title: Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
entries.snippet: Ukraine's president says Kyiv acted after 109 separate Russian aerial attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

entries.title: Man convicted of starting Palisades fire in Los Angeles
entries.snippet: The 30-year-old LA resident was convicted of arson leading to wildfires that killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,800 buildings.

entries.title: Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says
entries.snippet: Brussels sources had previously suggested the bloc might not apply the wider deal until fees were lowered for EU students in Britain.

entries.title: Ukrainian drones hit a Russian warship at a naval base in Libya, Zelenskyy says
entries.snippet: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault.

entries.title: Seniors embrace Tesla automated driving technology despite questions about safety
entries.snippet: Older drivers are using Tesla's automated driving technology to stay on the road longer. But safety experts warn the company may be over-selling what its cars can do.

entries.title: K is for kindness, but families worry the world has less of it
entries.snippet: A decade after first asking families about kindness, Sesame Workshop asked parents similar questions. They responded that their kids are getting kinder even as the wider world becomes less so.

entries.title: Mushroom supplements promise health benefits. What does the science say?
entries.snippet: Wellness influencers say mushroom supplements can help with your gut health, focus and immune system. Here is where research suggests there are some links.

entries.title: Let's talk turkey: Here's how Thanksgiving meal costs have changed this year
entries.snippet: Grocery costs have been on the rise, but food-price analysts say it's unclear if you'll spend more on the Thanksgiving meal this year. Some people are deciding not to host or are hosting fewer guests.

entries.title: Morning news brief
entries.snippet: A look at how artificial intelligence is affecting the economy, NATO to meet after Russian missiles hit Poland, negotiators fail to reach a deal as COP31 comes to an end.

entries.title: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly.
entries.snippet: It's not easy to retrieve foreign objects from animals once ingested. Some things can be grabbed using an endoscope. But if an item gets far into the intestinal tract, surgery isn't always possible.

entries.title: What it's like at a climate conference as talks collapse
entries.snippet: After two weeks of negotiations, international climate talks fail to reach an agreement. NPR's Rachel Waldholz was in Turkey for the conference.

entries.title: Philly festival-goers say pickles are a real big dill
entries.snippet: Influencer and pickle enthusiast Dan Pancoast gives a first hand account of the festivities at the "The Big Dill" festival in Philadelphia.

entries.title: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as the Israeli army pulls back
entries.snippet: In a pilot project in a village in southern Lebanon, Israeli forces have left and the Lebanese army moved it. But villagers who return find their houses wrecked.

entries.title: Lawyer: Father and daughter detained by ICE at Seattle airport were traveling to family baptism
entries.snippet: Other passengers boarding the Alaska Airlines flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday used their cellphones to film the father and daughter being detained by the officers, who were wearing unmarked jackets and khaki pants.

entries.title: In their own words: Leaders at UN climate talks discuss why negotiations ended without deal
entries.snippet: After reviewing a draft of the agreement released by co-host Turkey, a number of countries spoke up during the final meeting Sunday to say they couldn't accept a deal that failed to include wording on fossil fuels.

entries.title: Automation system problem at Delta causes flight delays as Americans travel for Thanksgiving
entries.snippet: Earlier Sunday, the Federal Aviation Administration issued about an hourlong ground stop to some flights into Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, which is Delta's hub and one of the busiest airports in the world.

entries.title: Today's Thanksgiving holiday was invented amid the Civil War to unite a divided country
entries.snippet: The idea of a straight line connecting that "first Thanksgiving" to Thanksgivings today is, in fact, an American myth.

entries.title: Appeals court says federal law requiring accommodations for pregnant workers is unconstitutional
entries.snippet: The appeals court said the act was unconstitutional because a majority of U.S. House members weren't physically present when it was approved as part of a spending package in December 2022.

entries.title: U.S. Army plans to invoke emergency provisions to detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
entries.snippet: Environmental groups criticized the government's move, decrying it as a maneuver to get around a court order and avoid public demands for safety and transparency.

entries.title: Poland says Russia allegedly twice tried to kill a Ukrainian American rapper
entries.snippet: Denmark is expected to ask the European Union this week for more decisive action stemming from the case, perhaps restricting Russian citizens from entering and traveling freely within the EU. Poland said it would support such measures.

entries.title: U.S. intelligence chief says Trump's description of Putin as a 'friend' is 'entirely appropriate'
entries.snippet: Clayton defended comments that Democrats have characterized as a betrayal of American values after Trump met with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping for rare three-way talks.

entries.title: Democrats clinch a historic House majority of at least 258 seats, the largest since 1992
entries.snippet: The 258-seat tally was reached Sunday after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.

entries.title: Scientists are fighting for their halted funds. Trust of Black communities may be harder to win back
entries.snippet: The study was among broader research into why Black Americans are twice as likely as their white peers to develop Alzheimer's, but the Trump administration abruptly halted it in its final stretch.

entries.title: French activists demand a tear gas suspension over reported menstrual changes
entries.snippet: Some women reported painful cramps, unexpected bleeding and disrupted menstrual cycles after exposure, and an advocacy group says it has collected more than 10,000 complaints.

entries.title: As AI detects flaws in computer systems, is it causing more tech outages and disruptions?
entries.snippet: AI rapidly identifies computer system vulnerabilities and companies are pressured to fix them. Experts say that might lead to unintended consequences, like tech outages.

entries.title: Mercury gets its first visitor in years as a pair of spacecraft loop into orbit
entries.snippet: BepiColombo is only the third spacecraft to visit Mercury — the sun's closest planet and barely bigger than our moon — and the first in more than a decade.

entries.title: UN climate talks break down over bitter disagreements on fossil fuels
entries.snippet: Expectations had already been low heading into the two-week negotiations in Turkey, but impasses over explicitly including fossil fuels and other issues, including money, proved irreconcilable.

entries.title: Immigration officers make arrests at Seattle airport in 'distressing' scene, delaying flight
entries.snippet: Video of the incident showed officers dragging away at least one person at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport as a woman screams that her daughter is being taken and she has a work permit.

entries.title: Why do people believe recent tech failures must be connected?
entries.snippet: Even without clear evidence, people drew connections between recent tech failures and outages. The way our brains and social media platforms work helps explain why.

entries.title: For families of the fallen, Trump's proposed arch casts a shadow over Arlington National Cemetery
entries.snippet: Trump's proposed 250-foot-tall arch could cast a long shadow on Arlington National Cemetery, with the potential to literally shade gravesites, disrupt solemn visits with the noise of construction and alter the carefully designed historic landscape of the nation's capital.

entries.title: Trump vows to work with Democrats to cap credit card interest rates at 10%
entries.snippet: The standard proposal would substantially reduce what credit card companies can charge customers. The median credit card interest rate is roughly 22.2%, according to an August survey by the New York Federal Reserve.

entries.title: AP source: FBI investigating apparent hack of its key national criminal justice database

entries.title: A doctor's guide to surviving — and enjoying — holiday feasting while on GLP‑1 medication
entries.snippet: Changes in appetite, smaller portion tolerance, limits on alcohol consumption, medication side effects and the desire to maintain progress can make navigating holiday traditions feel a little different.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: 'I've Lost Her Forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract
entries.snippet: For decades, Germans have known Hollywood's biggest stars through the same familiar voices. Now an AI clause in Netflix contracts is splitting the industry over whether it protects performers or exposes them.

entries.title: Budget cuts threaten Germany's fight against antisemitism and racism
entries.snippet: Numerous grassroots initiatives in Germany are facing funding cuts. Affected organizations are sounding the alarm, pointing to growing challenges posed by far-right extremism.

entries.title: What is crawling on Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch'?
entries.snippet: A new project and exhibition, "The Night Watch Lives," lifts the veil on the hidden world of microbes covering one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.

entries.title: Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?
entries.snippet: Germany plans to pay €10 a month into investment accounts for children to encourage long-term retirement saving. Economists say the measure may help build wealth but won't solve the country's pension funding challenge.

entries.title: NATO Parliamentary Assembly convenes amid Russian airspace violations
entries.snippet: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and German Foreign Minister Wadephul are set to address the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin while NATO representatives discuss Russian airspace violations in Brussels. DW has more.

entries.title: Ukraine updates: Kyiv claims strike that sank Russian ship off Libya
entries.snippet: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attack was carried out with Ukrainian-made naval drones. Meanwhile, NATO members are meeting to discuss an alleged Russian violation of Polish airspace. DW has more.

entries.title: Germany news: Metalworkers go on strike as pay dispute heats up
entries.snippet: Germany's biggest union is calling for more strikes over heated pay disputes with car makers like Mercedes and shipyards among the companies impacted. Meanwhile, a Berlin hospital fire leaves many injured. Follow DW.

entries.title: Rule-breaking is contagious — and good examples barely help
entries.snippet: Seeing someone break a rule makes people more likely to break it too, a new study finds, especially when the rule-breaker is on their side politically. Watching others behave well barely made a difference.

entries.title: Turkey: Thousands protest closure of critical media outlets
entries.snippet: Protesters gathered in Istanbul to show their support for press freedom in Turkey. The protest was called just days after the police raided Sozcu TV and arrested several senior staff members.

entries.title: Sudan: Drones hit UN building, residential area in Khartoum
entries.snippet: The drones targeted Khartoum, damaging a UN building in the residential area. The UN agency deemed it unacceptable that humanitarian workers were exposed to such danger.

entries.title: Libya: Suspected drone attack hits Russian ship in Benghazi
entries.snippet: A Russian vessel at an eastern Libyan naval base was hit by what is suspected to be a drone strike.

entries.title: Israel's Eisenkot condemns 'Jewish terrorism' in West Bank
entries.snippet: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has condemned a recent series of arson attacks in the occupied West Bank as "Jewish terrorism." Israeli authorities have opened an investigation into the incidents.

entries.title: COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use
entries.snippet: After two weeks of tough talks, the COP31 climate summit has closed without a consensus on how to quit fossil fuels or fund countries struggling to adapt to a hotter world.

entries.title: COP31: Climate deal 'not adopted,' summit president says
entries.snippet: The summit was extended as nations worked to reach a deal, but they couldn't agree on including fossil fuels. European nations, small island states and activists have criticized oil-producing countries for the impasse.

entries.title: Bayern Munich bosses under fire over Jamal Musiala comments
entries.snippet: Officials have publicly questioned whether Musiala will ever fully recover from a debilitating neurological condition and queried the validity of his contract, prompting criticism from fans, media and the FIFPRO union.

entries.title: China, ASEAN countries struggle over South China Sea code of conduct
entries.snippet: The Philippines wanted a South China Sea code of conduct in place by 2026. But persistent disagreements between China and ASEAN countries are slowing progress toward a deal.

entries.title: Inspired by Bernie Sanders: A German agency is using US-Style campaigning to boost the left in 2029
entries.snippet: "The Goodforces" wants to see a swing to the left in the 2029 German elections. The agency counts New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Bernie Sanders among its inspirations. Could it transform the political landscape?

entries.title: Germany news: IG Metall union calls for new 24-hour strike
entries.snippet: Germany's biggest single union, IG Metall, is calling on car and shipyard workers to strike amid a pay row. Meanwhile, Germany's president is setting off on an Africa trip. DW has more.

entries.title: US: ICE arrests 2 at Seattle airport in 'chilling' scenes — governor
entries.snippet: Washington's governor has denounced the arrests made by ICE officers at Seattle's airport, calling the incident "horrific."
